desc: Write and run a brute-force minimax solver for small N and small A_i to tabulate winners and infer a parity/count-based characterization.
Formalize the pass-pool reduction and show the outcome depends only on pool parity P and the count o of odd A_i.
Derive outcome rules for N=1 (always Fennec), N=2 (always Snuke), and N=3 (Fennec iff o≥1) separately.
Prove the general rule for N≥4: current player wins iff (P+o) is odd, via induction (base m=4 checked for all o-parity cases, induction for m≥5).
Implement a Python solution reading N and A from stdin applying: N=1→Fennec, N=2→Snuke, N=3→Fennec iff o≥1, N≥4→Fennec iff o odd.
Verify implementation on samples (1,9,2)→Fennec, (25,29)→Snuke, (1,9,2,25,2,9)→Snuke, plus edge cases all-odd/all-even/mixed.
